(2) `affine-block-address-lets-pipeliner-fly` — layout-for-addressability: the stored-block address `(b // 4) * 32 * SBN + ((b % 4) * 16) // 2 * SBN` is a STAIRCASE in the loop step — "an address the pipeliner cannot see as affine is not put in flight" (443ad4a, at-sha) — and since a stored macro block holds 8 tile rows the same address is simply `b * (8 * SBN)`: "8 bytes a block (low nibble: even input), 8 * SBN apart: an address the pipeliner follows" (nvfp4.py:312, in-source); distinct-from hoist-bit-address-out-of-packed-row-sweep (LICM hoists an INVARIANT; this makes an ADVANCING address affine so the pipeliner overlaps it); the priority datum "the weight traffic is what the step actually waits on" (message-only). Bevy worked out each entry's size by asking Rust how big the struct is, not how big the shader says it is. Normally both answers are 176, but w/ glam's scalar-math feature on, Rust packs the struct tighter, to 168 bytes. If a render phase draws exactly one mesh, the buffer comes out 168 bytes when the shader needs at least 176, and wgpu throws the binding-size error. With two or more meshes the buffer happens to be big enough, so the bug stays hidden.' THE LAW: when a host struct feeds a GPU buffer, the per-entry stride is the CONSUMER's (shader's) declared size, never the host's `size_of` — feature flags (glam scalar-math) and WGSL alignment rules can diverge the two views; the single-entry buffer is the LOUD case, the multi-entry case the SILENT one (spare bytes absorb the shortfall). Fix bounded (one line: the stride from the shader's size). In-lane: our WGSL instance/uniform buffers (seal-view ambient quads + grass instances ride vertex-stage tags with host-fed layouts; riir-shader gamefx). NotBenchable (correctness law; upstream ships no numbers). QUEUED for the cargo-quiet conversion batch (rider on the B211 entries host + gate test; quotes re-verified at conversion time).
- [x] **P50 — llama.cpp `358a420e` #30416 "graph: pad the KV dimension of the no-cache attention to 256": pad-at-the-producer + the probe-shape-class law. The CUDA kernels for head size 512 require a multiple of FATTN_KQ_STRIDE, so the op falls back to the CPU for most lengths, and the -fa auto probe (1 token) disables flash attention for such models. TWO faces: (1) **PAD-AT-THE-PRODUCER** — a fast kernel's stride/alignment contract on a DYNAMIC dimension must be met where the tensors are BUILT (the graph builder pads mask + K/V with zeros to the same shape the cached path's `get_n_kv` already produces), never repaired at dispatch — and the root cause is a PATH-VARIANT divergence (the cached path padded, the no-cache VARIANT skipped it: the sibling-transcription class); (2) **PROBE-SHAPE-CLASS** — the `-fa` auto probe measured at ONE token, a degenerate shape OUTSIDE the stride contract's domain, and concluded the fast arm unsupported for the model GLOBALLY: a capability probe must probe the shape class it gates, never a degenerate point (kin: B208's validated exact-shape admission; our `att_pf_fa` p≥128 engagement predicate is the same dispatch-agreement class). QUEUED for the cargo-quiet conversion batch (rider; quotes re-verified at conversion via the clone).

### #29882 transfer-question AUDIT VERDICT — exposure PRESENT in shape, adjudicated NO-GO as a standalone rung (amo-idle-audit29882, 2026-10-27T07:4xZ; answers the lead-3 transfer question above; read-only audit of riir-infer kernels, zero GPU, zero cargo)

**The riir-infer-gpu side is now VERIFIED.** The per-head q/k-norm kernels dispatch FIXED 256-thread workgroups on `head_dim`-wide rows — the #29882 pathological shape (fixed block > row length) is PRESENT on both GPU lanes:
- **Metal/CubeCL** (`crates/riir-infer-gpu/src/norms_cubecl.rs`): `rmsnorm_qk_fused_f32` (the decode Q+K single-dispatch, Issue-642 F4) + `RmsNormBatchedCubeCL` + `rmsnorm_zgate_fused_f32` (GDN out-norm+z-gate) — all `CubeDim::new_1d(256)` + a 256-slot 8-step smem tree; on qwen3.8 hd=128 rows, threads 128–255 idle (strided loop never entered) and tree step 1 folds `x + 0.0`. Contrast: the decode ATTENTION kernel in `qwen_attention_cubecl.rs` IS row-matched (`CubeDim::new_1d(head_dim)`) — the asymmetry is norm-only.
- **CUDA** (`cudarc_kernels/attention.rs` `rmsnorm_batched_f32`): "256 threads with strided accumulation", dispatch table `256 × 4` — same shape.
- **EDLM CubeCL fold** (`edlm_qkv_fold_f32`): ALREADY row-matched (`CubeDim::new_1d(128)` + 128-wide tree) — healthy, the in-repo proof the row-matched form works.
- **laya MSL**: N/A by architecture — laya serves gemma2/clef (gemma arch has no per-head learned qk-norm gamma; `query_pre_attn_scalar` + softcap instead). The "row-parallel softmax/LN" Pass-1 note is about the whole-hidden LN, a long-row kernel.

**Why NO-GO today (three structural reasons, each measured in-repo):**
1. **Decode is launch-bound, not bandwidth-bound.** The i1132 census ladder (Bench 1008) ranks launches (~17 µs class); the qk-norm launches sit inside i1135's attn-cluster rung whose shape is FUSION (the i1126 CUDA precedent fused the 5-launch chain). #29882's 4× read-bandwidth win applies to bandwidth-bound norm launches — not ~µs dispatch-floor launches.
2. **The bit-identity law pins the 256-slot tree pairing.** A naive row-matched 128-workgroup resize changes the summation order (step-1 pairing `x_i + x_{i+128}` vanishes) → G1 FAIL by the 1134/K3 precedents. The ONLY G1-legal form is the K3 trick already documented in `deltanet_rotation_cudarc.rs` L183-187: "the +0.0 folds of the 256-slot original are bit-neutral and skipped" — start the tree at the first nonzero pairing when dim ≤ 128. Real but nontrivial; bounded win at decode (launch floor caps it).
3. **The norm-fold lane just closed 7/7 NEGATIVE** (i1134, `ffb07bf`) — the census's norm classes are being adjudicated by fusion rungs and losing on measurement; a third norm-kernel rung (resize-shaped) would face the same launch-bound ceiling.

**Conditional re-arm:** a future floor census that shows per-head-norm EXEC (not launches) on the ladder — e.g. a large-context prefill posture where the `rows`-grid × 256-wg prefill batched norm becomes bandwidth-bound — re-opens the class with the K3 bit-neutral-skip as the implementation recipe. Until then this row is the answer; nothing filed in riir-infer (their tree is behind-origin + live lanes mid-flight; this snapshot row is the handoff — the i1135 lane gets the two load-bearing facts: the qk-norm launches are in its cluster, and any future resize must use the bit-neutral-skip form).

### kernel_opt pool (4 strong + 3 lower-tier)

1. **cubecl #1937** (`a5e8143`, 10-27 16:11 +07 — `RegisterBlock::partials`) — **contract-run partials deferred to the drain**: a register block contracting a K-lined rhs currently horizontal-sums each run into a one-value cell at EVERY step; opened with `partials()`, a cell is instead a line as wide as the run (one product a lane) and the lanes are summed ONCE when the block drains. Guard: only for a block the drain is the ONE reader of — `assert_whole_cells` refuses pre-drain reads (slice verbs + mma's lhs); `init` seeds first lane + identity in the rest; drain reduces each line after the plane/group fold. Reduction-deferral law with a provable sole-reader guard. HIGH. Dedup-at-mining vs the reduction/sum families.
2. **cubecl #1947 + #1936** (`f4055ea` + `01ae331` — the degenerate-dim pair) — **a dim of one element contributes NO layout facts**: (a) on a stride tie it sorts COARSEST, never innermost — a [k,1] view at strides [1,1] bound size-1 innermost, alignment admitted k-wide lines, and the binding then refused the width its routine was admitted at (4×1 rhs panic — admission/binding asymmetry); (b) `ElemAlignment` folded the size-1 dim's (stepping-nowhere) stride into the alignment → false alignment → every vector routine declined a legal row; (c) `Geometry::serves` skipped the dim in the line walk but not the outside-strides check. Law: the size-1 dim is invisible to stride-order, alignment, and line-admission alike, and EVERY checker must skip it symmetrically. Kin: B296 `vector-width-admission-checks-every-outer-stride` (admission-validity family). MED-HIGH.
3. **cubecl #1942** (`2774afa` — rejection persistence) — **a rejection seen while compiling a round STAYS a rejection, and patience skips what it never compiles**: the round compiles candidates together before measuring; the compile run discarded per-candidate results, so a candidate that rejected there was warmed up again and — when its profile then failed before its function ran — read as "executed but unmeasured", the round fell back on it and panicked running it for real. Fix: the compile run keeps the rejection on the candidate, the first pass leaves it out, and a patience-batched member its group skips is never compiled at all (lazy compile on reach). Tuner-phase state-consistency law, B284 autotune family. MED-HIGH.
4. **cubecl #1940** (`50041a2` — projection-aware stage fill) — a stage filled from a partition whose axes SHARE one physical axis must read THROUGH the projection: the straight fill handed the stage's logical coordinates to the source's physical layout position-by-position, putting an axis on the wrong physical stride (packed weight bound rows-as-[blocks, inside] staged its first row block linearly). Logical→physical coordinate mapping goes through the projection, never positionally, under shared-physical-axis. MED.

13. **TensorFold `893c8d7b`** — **cross-stream short-kernel consolidation through an address table (the shared-round law)**: 16 one-row streams each launching their own short kernels (30-layer conv + per-layer qk/attention/merge ×10) = 960 launches per forward "for little work each"; the fix runs each kernel ONCE per layer over EVERY row, reading per-stream cache addresses / row offsets / key counts from a table (`lfm2_segments.metal` + `segments.zig`); "each row's arithmetic is the per-stream kernel's, called through the same inline bodies" (the enabler commit `e4b874ec` inlines the kernel bodies so a consolidated kernel calls the IDENTICAL arithmetic — bit-equal replacement, float64 attention + host conv-replay contract). Regime gates preserved: >8-row streams keep their own 16-row tile folds; prompt calls and one-stream windows keep their per-stream launches. RESIDENCY RIDER (the subtle half): "a kernel that reaches them through the table alone may read them before they are resident" — every table-reached cache buffer must be DECLARED to the encoder; a new stream's caches join the residency set only at its next flush. Dedup-at-mining vs the B105 gpu-resident routing (device-side scheduling between grouping and down), the B293 co-residency-capped-launch host, and the launch-count families (the b10826 GDN conv-chain fusion kinship: consolidation across stream boundaries is the sibling of consolidation across kernel boundaries). HIGH.
14. **TensorFold `85571acb`** — **MMA-window dispatch admission by output-count floor**: the dense twin's MMA-window kernel (one threadgroup per 16 outputs over every row) is admitted ONLY for matrices of ≥4,096 outputs — "a 2,048-wide matrix then has 128 threadgroups and runs slower than the scalar twin's 4-row passes"; the 6,144-wide short-conv input and the head KEEP the window. Per-MATRIX admission, not per-shape ("the load check runs each matrix's twin at every width"); the twin contract now also serves 16 rows of 6,144 from 2,048. The occupancy-starvation pole of the admission family: B296 owns width-validity, B297 owns capacity-derived tiles, THIS owns the occupancy floor below which the vector kernel loses to the scalar twin. MED-HIGH.
15. **uzu `13b138eb` (#1022)** — **mode-specialized merged kernel (the weaver fusion)**: two adjacent per-step selection kernels (`weaver_top_children`, `weaver_frontier_select`) merged into ONE `weaver_select` kernel with `#[specialize] mode: WeaverSelectionMode` (a compile-time function-constant) and per-mode `#[optional]` parameters (`#[optional(mode != Frontier)] residual_logits…`) — each specialization's compiled kernel only reads/writes its own surface; −15 dispatches, ~+2% draft. The atom: N adjacent small kernels in a per-step loop sharing most inputs become one mode-specialized kernel; unused params null out per specialization. Kin: the p11 addendum's llama.cpp TOP_K_MASK function-constant row (dropping unused graph paths) + B293's pipeline-cache-key-covers-every-function-constant (every cache tier keys the constant). Dedup-at-mining vs the fusion-admission + dispatch-count families. MED.

### serving / measurement pool (3)

17. **TensorFold `622a54af`** — **the prefill interference budget (serving realism)**: short prompts (≤512 uncached rows) fill back-to-back and pause decoding streams up to lanes×512 rows; `TENSORFOLD_PREFILL_BUDGET=N` bounds the rows a fill visit consumes WHILE a stream could decode, then "the decoders' round goes first"; rows filled while nothing decodes don't count (progress-based accounting); the anti-starvation clause — "a long prompt that has waited preference_rounds choices takes the visit's first call, so short arrivals cannot spend every budget before it"; a no-progress call spends the whole budget. Directly applicable to OUR serving/lane-host benches with synthetic load. Kin: vllm #64167 (the p11 Zipf-skew row — same bench-realism family, scheduler side). MED-HIGH.
18. **TensorFold `afa4fa38` + `d22d7049` + `10aac5e5` (the spill-I/O trio, one row)** — **spill costs leave the engine thread's critical path**: (a) write-behind — cache images staged before entry release, written+fsync'd as PRIVATE temp files on a bounded I/O worker, generations published ON the engine (atomic swap), deletion/shutdown fenced (`TENSORFOLD_ROWS_SYNC=1` the synchronous oracle); (b) read-ahead — a queued request's disk state read into host memory on the I/O thread while other streams decode; a failed/late/mismatched read drops and admission re-reads synchronously (restored bytes = the synchronous read's); two requests for one state read it once; (c) ordering + bounded teardown — read I/O kept separate from write I/O, a compatible staged save waited before planning a queued restore under ONE wait bound, stop-deadline cancels + detaches blocked readers retaining permits. Serving-category law (not kernel_opt, not rust_perf mechanics). MED.

### kernel_opt pool (3 STRONG staged + 1 rust_perf + 3 rider tier)

- **S1 `mma-accumulator-run-as-one-operand-depth-matches-instruction` (B+, STRONG DISTINCT — cubecl `07cd07a` #1975 + `4549408` #1971, the #1966 series, MIT OR Apache-2.0)**: the accumulator-operand family's RUN-DEPTH face. Commit verbatim: "A product that contracts its own output, as an attention's value contracts its score, read each accumulator as the A of an instruction as deep as the accumulator is wide: m16n8 scores fed m16n8k8, which runs at half the rate of m16n8k16 on an RTX PRO 6000 (1.97 ns a call per SM for either)." — "`accumulator_as_a` becomes `accumulators_as_a`: a run of accumulators along the contraction, laid one after another into the A operand, which is where the manual-mma layouts put them for 16-bit operands." The law: when a product's output IS its contraction operand (self-contracting attention value∘score), a SINGLE accumulator's width sets the MMA's K-depth — m16n8k8 runs at HALF the m16n8k16 rate; laying a RUN of accumulators consecutively into the A operand makes the instruction depth = the run depth, recovering the k16 rate with the same bits. KINSHIP (adjudicated in-greps): `mma-accumulate-into-resident-accumulator-c-operand` (B205, gpu_75) owns the C-OPERAND alias (accumulation PLACEMENT, temp+add-back elimination) — THIS owns the A-OPERAND RUN-DEPTH law (instruction-RATE recovery by run depth); the source itself names the boundary — `MmaData::mma` "loses its accumulator arm" (the B205 shape retired at the cubek layer) while the run form is the new content; compose, never merge. Measured basis source-reported (the 1.97 ns/call/SM rate pair — the depth-pairing decision is the content). Category B. NotBenchable here (RTX PRO 6000 + cubecl tile IR; the admission shape + the depth-vs-width pairing are CPU-testable and ARE the fixtures). Conversion: quotes re-verified at the pin at claim time (clone `.raw/` owed).
- **S2 `barriers-declared-before-slots-one-free-run` (B, STRONG DISTINCT — same commits, the `Stages::free` atom)**: the SMEM FRAGMENTATION face. Commit verbatim: "a ring's barriers are declared before its slots' data — `Stages::free` hands a ring's shared memory to what the kernel declares after the walk, which the allocator gives only a run of freed memory. Each slot declared its data then its full/empty barriers, which stay in use, so a ring filled by the copy engine freed its slots as pieces cut apart by live barriers: an attention cube's 64 KiB partial fit none of them and was placed after the ring, 131 KiB in all, past an RTX PRO 6000's 99." The law: in a stage/ring whose slots are freed while their barriers stay live, DECLARATION ORDER is an allocation-fragmentation control — declare the long-lived barriers FIRST as one run and the data after, or the allocator's contiguous-run policy fragments the free space until the placement overflows the platform SMEM ceiling (64→131 KiB past a 99 KiB limit). KINSHIP: lifecycle-disjoint-intermediates-union-smem-scratch (B234, gpu_94) owns lifetime-disjoint SHARING; the smem-interleave legality face (B234 rider) owns free-legality (barrier-dominates-first-use); the smem-budget family owns sizing — NONE owns declaration ORDER as the fragmentation remedy; the overflow-at-placement failure shape is the outcome class. Category E (allocation/smem). NotBenchable (SMEM placement policy; the order-vs-fragmentation shape is fixture-testable).
- **S4 `warp-per-row-small-blocks-cta-under-load-law` (B, DISTINCT — PrismML fork `9d9efea` #415, the NEW SCORED-TAG tip `prism-b10831`)**: the NEW TAG's headline commit, body verbatim: "The generic loop strides the 128-weight blocks over all threads of the CTA, so at K <= 4096 (<= 32 blocks per row) only the first warp loads. Give each warp its own row and let the lanes stride the blocks, with the same per-row accumulation order and epilogue, so outputs are unchanged." In-diff admission: `if constexpr (small_k && type == GGML_TYPE_PTQ1_0 && ncols_dst == 1 && !y_soa && nwarps > 1 && rows_per_cuda_block == nwarps)` + `if (ids != nullptr && blocks_per_row_x <= warp_size)` — the guard requires blocks_per_row ≤ warp_size so every lane holds exactly one block; per-row accumulation order + the same warp_reduce_sum butterfly = bit-identical. The law: when blocks-per-work-unit < threads-per-CTA, a whole-CTA block-stride loop idles (warps 1..N load nothing); the remedy is warp-per-ROW at small K, admitted only while blocks_per_row ≤ warp_size (the one-block-per-lane floor that keeps the butterfly). LEAGUE NOTE: this is the opponent's NEWEST scored tag (b10831 > b10828, ~10.7 h after the 10-29b sweep saw b10828 as top) — league disposition rides the riir-ai watch (L1 below). Kinship: the planar/PT family (B180 planar-transposed-activation — the `ptq1_0_pt_block_dot` call IS the planar-block form) + the warp-partition reduction family (gpu_09) — the ADMISSION FLOOR (blocks_per_row ≤ warp_size as the idle-threshold crossover, on the MUL_MAT_ID/ids path) is the unowned content. Category D. NotBenchable (fork CUDA; no numbers in-commit; sm_89 impact untested upstream).
- **S3 `metadata-count-query-builds-no-structure` (B−, rust_perf complexity — cubecl `07cd07a`, the `StageStorage::bytes` atom, same series)**: commit verbatim: "a stage's size is counted without building its projections — `StageStorage::bytes` built the whole `StageForm` a stage is laid out in, projections and all, to read its line count, and routines ask it in every prepare, at every candidate line width of every stage. The count only reads the form's extents and its rows' padding: `StageForm::dense_cells` computes those two through the same functions `dense` does, and nothing else." The law: a size/metadata QUERY on a hot path (every prepare × every candidate line width × every stage) must read the extents the answer derives from, never construct the full artifact the query merely describes — build-only-to-count is the anti-shape. Kinship: the hoist/memo family is adjacent (compute-once) but the atom is narrower — do not BUILD for a COUNT. rust_perf domain, category complexity. NotBenchable (compile-time cost; the count-vs-build split is fixture-testable).

Body verbatim: "The seam exchanges whole output rows instead of K halves: rank r owns 2,560 of the 5,120 output columns (8,704 of 17,408 for the down projection), reduces over the full K on its own rank, and `pair_gather` copies whole rows in bf16 without doing any arithmetic, so no exchange rounds or sums a partial product across ranks." THE LAW: when a matmul is partitioned across ranks joined by a copy-capable exchange, partition by OUTPUT rows (each rank owns disjoint outputs and reduces the full K locally) — never by K halves, which forces every exchange to carry PARTIAL PRODUCTS (extra reduce rounds + cross-rank floating-point summation error); the copy-only exchange moves FINISHED values and "carries no sums and no accumulator's error". SECOND INSTANCE SAME WINDOW (corroboration, different repo-layer): TF `fccb46a` (fabric/tp) — "the multirank probe vote is keepIfAll, with a test that one rank's mismatch drops the wire on every rank". A sampled stream's drafts carry no head chance (GLM gives them 1), so it verified the deepest window each round: at TP=3 a sampled chat reply drafted 3 a round where its rates chose fewer, and lost 1.7 to 2.0% at one stream. headDepth and depth now keep the rates' depth for a sampled stream under a floor; greedy streams draft the most as before." Decision content: a confidence-gated policy must PRESERVE the non-gated lane's own policy (sampled streams have no head chances — the floor must not convert their depth choice to always-max); the general form: a gate added for one lane class must not override a second class's independent policy — measured −1.7..−2.0% when it did. (2) `affine-block-address-lets-pipeliner-fly` — layout-for-addressability: the stored-block address `(b // 4) * 32 * SBN + ((b % 4) * 16) // 2 * SBN` is a STAIRCASE in the loop step — "an address the pipeliner cannot see as affine is not put in flight" (443ad4a, at-sha) — and since a stored macro block holds 8 tile rows the same address is simply `b * (8 * SBN)`: "8 bytes a block (low nibble: even input), 8 * SBN apart: an address the pipeliner follows" (nvfp4.py:312, in-source); distinct-from hoist-bit-address-out-of-packed-row-sweep (LICM hoists an INVARIANT; this makes an ADVANCING address affine so the pipeliner overlaps it); the priority datum "the weight traffic is what the step actually waits on" (message-only).
